The page migration code employs try_to_unmap() to try and unmap the source
page.  This is accomplished by using rmap_walk to find all vmas where the
page is mapped.  This search stops when page mapcount is zero.  For shared
PMD huge pages
column2: the page map count is always 1 no matter the number of

column1: mappings.  Shared mappings are tracked via the reference count of the PMD
page.  Therefore
column2: try_to_unmap stops prematurely and does not completely

column1: unmap all mappings of the source page.
This problem can result is data corruption as writes to the original
source page can happen after contents of the page are copied to the target
page.  Hence
This problem was originally seen as DB corruption of shared global areas
after a huge page was soft offlined due to ECC memory errors.  DB
developers noticed they could reproduce the issue by (hotplug) offlining
memory used to back huge pages.  A simple testcase can reproduce the
problem by creating a shared PMD mapping (note that this must be at least
PUD_SIZE in size and PUD_SIZE aligned (1GB on x86))
migrate_pages() to migrate process pages between nodes while continually
writing to the huge pages being migrated.
To fix
column2: have the try_to_unmap_one routine check for huge PMD sharing by

column1: calling huge_pmd_unshare for hugetlbfs huge pages.  If it is a shared
mapping it will be 'unshared' which removes the page table entry and drops
the reference on the PMD page.  After this
mmu notifiers are called before locking page tables
sure of PMD sharing until page tables are locked.  Therefore
the possibility of PMD sharing before locking so that notifiers can
prepare for the worst possible case.
